# Evaluation results (generated by eval/evaluate.py)

30 ideas, one known target paper each, drawn at random from the 1,944-paper store. Rewrites by gpt-5.4-mini with the app's own prompt.
Casual descriptions share a median of 2 content words with their target (max 5); 3/30 share none.

## 1. Does the target paper come back? (good rewrites)

| search | hit@5 | hit@10 | MRR |
|---|---|---|---|
| vector-only (casual words) | 19/30 | 23/30 | 0.540 |
| rewrite-only | 24/30 | 25/30 | 0.769 |
| merged: min (current app) | 24/30 | 25/30 | 0.769 |
| merged: RRF (k=60) | 22/30 | 23/30 | 0.662 |
| merged: weighted 0.5/0.5 | 24/30 | 25/30 | 0.676 |
| merged: weighted 0.7 user / 0.3 rewrite | 22/30 | 23/30 | 0.631 |
| gate (drop rewrite if > 0.56) + min | 24/30 | 25/30 | 0.769 |
| _reference: technical description, vector-only_ | 30/30 | 30/30 | 0.983 |

In the current min() fusion, 93% of top-5 papers get their score from the rewrite, not the user's words: rewrite distances run lower (median nearest 0.337 vs 0.491), so min() is effectively rewrite-only.

## 2. When the rewrite is bad

hit@5 with each kind of rewrite, and how many of the top-5 slots (out of 150) are taken by papers that are not even in the casual query's top 20, i.e. pulled in by the rewrite alone.

| fusion | hit@5 good | hit@5 mild drift | hit@5 total drift | rewrite-only slots: good / mild / total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| merged: min (current app) | 24/30 | 22/30 | 9/30 | 41 / 50 / 128 |
| merged: RRF (k=60) | 22/30 | 21/30 | 6/30 | 2 / 10 / 69 |
| merged: weighted 0.5/0.5 | 24/30 | 25/30 | 6/30 | 11 / 19 / 92 |
| merged: weighted 0.7 user / 0.3 rewrite | 22/30 | 24/30 | 18/30 | 3 / 7 / 17 |
| gate (drop rewrite if > 0.56) + min | 24/30 | 20/30 | 19/30 | 41 / 33 / 0 |
| _vector-only, no rewrite_ | 19/30 | 19/30 | 19/30 | 0 / 0 / 0 |

Verdict changes caused by the rewrite (vs. vector-only verdict), out of 30:

| fusion | good rewrite | mild drift | total drift |
|---|---|---|---|
| merged: min (current app) | 27 | 26 | 25 |
| merged: weighted 0.5/0.5 | 21 | 15 | 16 |
| merged: weighted 0.7 user / 0.3 rewrite | 14 | 12 | 22 |

- merged: min (current app): with a totally wrong rewrite, 22/30 ideas get VERY CLOSE MATCH for a paper outside the casual top 20
- gate (drop rewrite if > 0.56) + min: with a totally wrong rewrite, 0/30 ideas get VERY CLOSE MATCH for a paper outside the casual top 20
- merged: weighted 0.7 user / 0.3 rewrite: with a totally wrong rewrite, 0/30 ideas get VERY CLOSE MATCH for a paper outside the casual top 20

## 3. Rewrite drift: cosine distance between the user's idea and the rewrite

| pair | min | median | max |
|---|---|---|---|
| my technical description (human, faithful) | 0.378 | 0.541 | 0.730 |
| good LLM rewrite | 0.197 | 0.312 | 0.520 |
| LLM asked to drift (mild) | 0.231 | 0.416 | 0.644 |
| another idea's rewrite (total drift) | 0.601 | 0.805 | 1.009 |

Any cutoff between 0.52 and 0.60 separates good from totally drifted rewrites perfectly. The gate uses the midpoint, **X = 0.56**: keeps 30/30 good, rejects 30/30 total drift and 5/30 mild drift.
Rewrites that moved the target up more than 20 places: 3; their idea-rewrite distance: median 0.475 (max 0.495) vs 0.277 for the rest. Faithful human restatements exceed 0.56 in 12/30 cases, so the gate is tuned to this LLM's wording style.
Relative check: a good rewrite is closer to its own idea than to any of the other 29 ideas in 30/30 cases.

## 4. Casual vs technical wording: the distance gap

| | casual | technical | gap (casual - technical) |
|---|---|---|---|
| distance to nearest paper, median | 0.491 | 0.257 | 0.227 (sd 0.076, range 0.077 to 0.390) |
| distance to the target paper, median | 0.527 | 0.257 | 0.265 |

Verdict agreement with the technical description's verdict (30 ideas):

- casual, vector-only, current thresholds: 0/30
- casual + good rewrite (current app with a key): 22/30
- casual, thresholds shifted by the median gap (0.227): 28/30
- cost of that shift for someone who writes technically without a key: their verdict changes in 1/30 cases
- nonsense queries still OUT OF SCOPE after the shift: 0/6

Same test with each target paper hidden (an idea whose exact paper isn't in the store):

- casual vs technical agreement, current thresholds: 13/30; shifted: 7/30
- cost of the shift for technical writers without a key: verdict changes in 22/30 cases

Verdict distribution (casual / technical / casual+rewrite): VERY CLOSE MATCH 0/29/22; CROWDED 13/1/7; RELATED WORK EXISTS 13/0/1; LOOKS OPEN 4/0/0; OUT OF SCOPE 0/0/0
